newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler - sales to grow to 130 bln by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Daimler - sales to grow to 130 bln by 2000.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG sales are likely to climb to around 130 billion marks by 2000 from near 106 billion marks now, chief financial officer Manfred Gentz told the German daily Handelsblatt.
In an interview with the newspaper, Gentz said the company also planned fixed asset investments of more than six billion marks this year.
Gentz said that he did not expect to raise more capital this year. "We have no plans for a classic capital increase this year and probably not in 1998."

The Daimler CFO also added that the stronger dollar should help the company's profits. He said that from a theoretical standpoint, an increase in the dollar of 10 pfennigs should boost operating profit by around 800 million marks.
Gentz said that figure, however, was not hard and fast because of the impact of price pressures abroad and foreign exchange hedging.
Over the long term, Gentz said Daimler based its business projections on a dollar/mark level of 1.40. In morning trade in Frankfurt on Friday, the dollar stood at 1.63 marks.
